title: Adult walking competence and motor-excitability bridge

scope.claimBoundary: Published values constrain active straight walking bouts, leg-joint cycle frequency, and slow-unit readiness. They do not specify spontaneous chamber-average speed, navigation success, or a complete free-walking muscle transfer. The motor-excitability and planar traction equations are disclosed engineering bridges.

sources.title: Quantification of gait parameters in freely walking wild type and sensory deprived Drosophila melanogaster
A size principle for recruitment of Drosophila leg motor neurons

observations.interpretation: Tonic slow-unit activity supports resting force/posture and readiness; it is not translated into a constant body velocity.

sources.title: Inter-leg coordination in the control of walking speed in Drosophila
sources.license: bibliographic metadata and abstract only; source article not redistributed

observations.speedControl: Walking speed is controlled predominantly through step frequency.
observations.coordination: High speed favors tripod coordination; slower walking can show tetrapod and wave-like patterns.

derivedConstraints.derivation: 28 mm/s multiplied by the 0.06 s representative plateau period. This is a planar advance scale, not a measured stride length for each leg.

engineeringBridge.problemObservation: Across 30 seconds of default-room Balanced BANC execution, every identified leg-motor population produced zero spikes. Mean normalized subthreshold activations were 0.00045 to 0.00413, while the global CNS homeostatic multiplier rose to 4.6374. The homogeneous LIF model therefore under-drives known heterogeneous motor physiology.

motorDecoder.spikeEvidence: 1 - exp(-(population spike rate * output gain) / 4.2 Hz)
motorDecoder.subthresholdEvidence: 1 - exp(-(population normalized activation * configured subthreshold gain * output gain) / 0.16)
motorDecoder.zeroRule: Exactly zero spike and subthreshold evidence produces exactly zero leg drive.
motorDecoder.evidenceClass: provisional engineering compensation for absent motor-neuron-specific intrinsic physiology

plant.activeGaitFrequencyHz: clamp(10 + 7 * coordination evidence + 3 * mean leg evidence, 10, 20) when either evidence is nonzero; otherwise 0
plant.targetSpeedMmPerSecond: direction * gait frequency * 1.68 mm/cycle * measured stance traction
plant.zeroRule: Coordination may advance phase but cannot generate traction or translation without identified leg evidence.

ingestionSemantics.reason: Weak neural proboscis evidence remains observable but is not rendered as sustained extension. Feeding/drinking requires matching mouth contact; stronger output without contact is labeled probing.

qualificationPolicy.seedBoundary: Seeds are deterministic initial-condition replicates, not independent animals.
requiredChecks: zero-output and coordination-only body states remain exactly immobile
bare-floor proboscis output is labeled as an attempt, never ingestion
resource consumption requires matching mouth contact and neural attempt
actual multi-seed Balanced BANC default-room paths demonstrate locomotor competence
active speeds and gait frequencies are checked against the published bout envelopes
turning and coverage arise without target coordinates or post-connectome steering
pauses remain permitted and resource encounter is not required for every seed
neural and motor outputs remain bounded

knownLimitations: The calibration does not make the homogeneous LIF model neuron-specific.
Subthreshold membrane activation is a population mean and not an intracellular motor-neuron recording.
The shared gait phase and planar stance traction are transitional engineering mechanics.
The active-bout speed envelope must not be applied to pauses or interpreted as spontaneous chamber-average speed.
A resource encounter is evidence of embodied sensory geometry only; failure to encounter one is not automatically a locomotor failure.
No target coordinate, ideal action, constant forward floor, scripted food bearing, or anti-circling correction is introduced.
